---
type: reference/types/design-proposal.md
description: "Proposal: remove the Source register's duplicated path inventory so later analysis findings can cite any inspected path in their frozen source"
---

# Source registers without duplicated path inventories

## Problem

The boundary author lists source paths before the specialists discover all
paths needed for their findings. Judges have treated that list as an exhaustive
inventory, making source discovery a defect the record loop cannot repair. Each
finding already carries a source ID and commit-relative path, and the source
ID fixes its repository and revision.

## Current state (as of 2026-10-01)

The source contract requires a Source register with inspected paths and
citation anchors, and requires each source-dependent finding to name a source
ID and local anchor that exists at the frozen revision. It does not explicitly
make the register's anchor list an exhaustive citation whitelist. In fresh Luna
run `AAS-2026-10-01-instinctual-memory-01`, the boundary listed three
implementation anchors and scoped the source unit to modules including the
later-inspected paths. Both record judges nevertheless required those further
paths in the register. Reconciliation could not amend the boundary, and final
verification stopped the run before synthesis.

The runtime and source register were frozen at the same clean commit. The
stop included the judges' inventory interpretation, not an unknown repository revision.
The final reconciliation also lost a formal amendment and conflict marker;
removing the inventory would not repair those independent faults. Another
trial altered a generated quotation while copying it; that is a separate
retained-content integrity issue.

## Forces

Keep source identity, revision, evidence layer and inspected scope visible.
Every finding must remain traceable to an existing path at the frozen revision.
Avoid an inventory whose author cannot yet know later discoveries, and avoid
another correction route solely to maintain duplicated information. Source
membership and quotation occurrence do not establish semantic support.

## Options and operative paths

### Remove the register's path inventory

Keep source identity, revision, evidence layer and inspected scope in the
register; retain the full local anchor on each finding. The source contract
would stop requiring a second list of those paths. Workers would consume that
rule as authoring authority, and validators and judges would resolve the
finding's source ID and path against the frozen source rather than a copied
inventory. Existing source-resolution and quote-generation code supplies the
revision boundary; no consumer would treat mere file existence as support.

### Register every source path before analysis

The boundary job could enumerate all paths up front. Later workers and judges
would consume that inventory as their allowed citation surface. This preserves
the current rule, but increases boundary work and context, and mixes inspected
anchors with files that were merely enumerated.

### Add boundary correction after report verification

The judge could return missing paths to a boundary author. Code would consume
that return as authority to change the Source register and repeat affected
checks. This preserves the inventory at the cost of another correction route
and a mutable boundary document. The frozen source revision would remain fixed.

## Adoption criteria

The operator must choose whether register membership means a frozen source
unit or an exhaustively enumerated file surface. A trial must demonstrate that
a specialist can cite a newly inspected path at the same revision without
reopening the boundary, while an unknown source ID or nonexistent path is
still refused. Quote-copy integrity and formal reconciliation retention remain
separate decisions. This proposal does not change the shipped contract.

---
description: "Proposal: Commonplace's strategy as a testable conjecture — support for search judgments and commitments built for theory building generalizes to other kinds of knowledge work more economically than per-kind tools — with its defeaters"
type: reference/types/design-proposal.md
tags: [self-improving-systems, learning-theory]
---

# Reusable commitment support as the route from theory building to other knowledge work

## Current state (as of 2026-10-30)

- Commonplace's declared objective is more useful and better-warranted
  knowledge work per unit of human judgment
  ([Commonplace as an instrument](../commonplace-as-an-instrument.md)).
  Its strategy is stated in pieces: build a theory builder and test whether
  it learns; start from a running system because use supplies selection
  where no fixed oracle exists; invest in machinery because an improvement
  is paid once and reused. No artifact states the step from that program to
  other kinds of knowledge work, or what would show the step is uneconomical.
- The machinery that exists serves theory building in a KB: types and
  collection contracts, validators, review gates, hash-pinned review results,
  connect and ingest skills, the search-control and commitment notes, and
  the draft refinement interface (derive, compare, locate, revise,
  evaluate, apply) in the
  `theory-refinement-interface` workshop, which is not promoted.
- Transfer has not been demonstrated: "Both instances were authored inside
  the system that states the claim and assessed by nobody outside it"
  (instrument note). No second kind of knowledge work runs on the
  machinery. The
  `first-downstream-run` workshop holds the template for an outside
  KB-building trial, not yet handed over.
- The library's generality rule for the KB framework is to demote closed
  taxonomies to guarded defaults and gate universality on heterogeneous
  worked cases
  ([universal knowledge framework](../../theory/a-universal-knowledge-framework-demotes-content-taxonomies-to-defaults.md));
  ADR 042 is its implemented instance (text contract plus profiles).
- The only recorded shared engine built ahead of its second consumer was
  retired on its carrying cost (ADR 113 to ADR 118); the
  [codify-versus-LLM](../../theory/codify-versus-llm-decision-heuristics.md)
  note's "Stake and odds" section now carries that lesson.
- The direction of development is toward unattended pipelines
  (the `review-on-workjig` and `recurring-task-runner` workshops), where
  computation cost becomes the binding comparison for controllers.

## Problem

The work-level claim is held: open-ended work allocates search before
decisive evidence, keeps "worth investigating" apart from "warranted to
adopt", retains commitments by their ground-truth status, and converts
stable patterns into routines. What is not held is the architecture-level
claim the program rests on: that *reusable* support for these operations,
built for theory building, is an economical route to supporting other
kinds of open-ended knowledge work (scientific investigation, software
architecture, legal drafting, exploration). The claim is implicit in the
lead article's bet and in the software-house endpoint, but nowhere stated
with its universality axis declared or its defeaters named. Without that
statement, every success inside the KB reads as support and no failure
reads as refutation.

The brief that posed this names the endpoint "a general computational
environment". The library does not use that term and this proposal does
not introduce it; the conjecture is stated as
generalization from theory building to other kinds of knowledge work, with
the [software house](../../theory/definitions/software-house.md) as the
software-specific case of the endpoint.

## The conjecture

Stated in the form the library already uses for factories,
`F_P = configure(G, K_P)`
([agentic substrate](../../theory/agentic-substrate-needs-family-specific-machinery-to-be-a-factory.md)):

> There is general machinery **G** — support for making, recording,
> criticizing, routing and retaining search judgments and commitments —
> such that each kind of open-ended knowledge work **P** is served by
> `configure(G, K_P)`, where **K_P** is that kind's domain knowledge
> (its types, oracles, routines and vocabulary). Building and improving
> **G** once, and acquiring **K_P** per kind, costs less over the horizon
> than building per-kind tools, and the cost of the shared abstractions
> stays below the duplication they remove.

Three held results give it its economic form. A machinery improvement is
paid once and reused by every later episode, so **G**'s return grows with
the number of kinds and episodes that use it
([machinery investment](../../theory/an-optimal-long-run-learning-strategy-invests-in-its-own-machinery.md)).
The expensive part per kind is acquiring **K_P**, not constructing
machinery
([factory construction does not establish knowledge acquisition](../../theory/factory-construction-does-not-establish-knowledge-acquisition.md)),
so a shared **G** does not remove the hard work; it removes rebuilding the
easy part. And conversion of a kind's stable patterns into routines is the
mechanism by which that kind's work gets cheaper, and the conversion
machinery (observe, commit when stable, relax on failure signals, price
the stake) is the same for every kind.

What **G** is, in the library's terms, is theory-building machinery: the
operations a [theory builder](../../theory/definitions/theory-builder.md)
performs (propose, derive, criticize, locate blame, revise, select, change
the machinery) together with the search control that decides which of
them runs next. Whether theory building is the layer every open-ended
kind of knowledge work shares is a separate question, open in `kb/log.md`;
the comparison below does not depend on it.

**Universality axis, declared** (per the
[universality-axis note](../../theory/universal-software-factory-needs-a-declared-universality-axis.md)):

- Axis: constructional expressivity of **G** across kinds, *plus* reuse
  economy. Not production-knowledge acquisition reach: whether computation
  acquires **K_P** from evidence is the program's separate bet, and this
  proposal allows **K_P** to be human-supplied.
- Covered class: kinds of knowledge work in which consequential branches
  are generated during the work and results accumulate across bounded
  episodes. Routine work, where no search judgment is uncertain, is out.
- Supplied inputs: **K_P** by people initially; problems and acceptance
  judgments by users throughout.
- Adequacy: the declared objective, measured as the
  [ablation proposal](../proposals/ablation-baselines-for-the-declared-objective.md)
  measures it, per kind.
- Human boundary: internal production roles may be human in **K_P**
  acquisition; the conjecture is about **G**'s reuse, not about autonomy.
- Horizon and resources: stated per test; the claim is comparative over a
  horizon long enough for **G**'s reuse to amortize.

## Design space

Three options for how **G** comes to exist. The proposal does not choose.

1. **Interface first.** Promote the refinement interface and the
   search-control and commitment machinery as the declared **G**, then
   configure a second kind against it. Cheapest to state, dearest if the
   interface was shaped by theory building alone: a description that
   contains its target is weak expressivity (universality-axis note).
2. **Second kind first, extract later.** Serve a second kind with the
   existing machinery as it stands, allow bespoke additions, and extract
   **G** from what two kinds in fact shared. This is
   [progressive constraining](../../theory/progressive-constraining-commits-only-after-patterns-stabilize.md)
   applied to the architecture: commit the shared layer only after the
   pattern stabilizes across kinds. It pays observation time and risks the
   second kind's additions entrenching before extraction.
3. **No shared layer.** Commonplace stays a KB framework; other kinds use
   generic harness features and their own tools. This is the rival the
   conjecture must beat on total cost, and the option the bootstrap note's
   last failure condition names ("a more direct learning method achieves
   better results at comparable total cost").

Option 2 is consistent with every rule the library already applies to
itself (demote taxonomies to defaults, promote on stable repetition, size
the stake to the stated odds) and with the ADR 113 lesson. That is a
reason to expect it to be chosen, not a decision.

## Forces

- **Entrenchment and coordination value.** A shared **G** earns its cost
  only under an enduring constraint, scoped transfer evidence, or
  coordination value
  ([entrenchment](../../theory/current-task-fit-alone-does-not-warrant-costly-entrenchment.md),
  [coordination value](../../theory/definitions/coordination-value.md)).
  Adoption by more kinds raises migration cost without demonstrating
  transfer.
- **Carrying cost of shared abstractions.** The one recorded case (ADR 113)
  had consistency machinery exceed the domain logic it served. The
  natural-language analogue is the
  [checked-inline-blocks](../proposals/checked-inline-blocks-for-shared-instruction-text.md)
  problem: one authoritative definition against literal, sufficient text in
  each bounded context.
- **Expressiveness is not economy.** "An operation that is possible but
  too costly is different from one the permitted machinery cannot express"
  ([fixed-model house](../../theory/a-fixed-model-house-must-retain-missing-procedures-for-theory-use.md)).
  A **G** whose operations are available by interpretation for every
  kind establishes expressivity, not the conjecture.
- **Preferential codification.** A shared layer takes the predictable
  parts of each kind; the kind keeps the hard parts
  ([preferential codification](../../theory/codifying-predictable-choices-leaves-agents-with-less-predictable-work.md)).
  Success of **G** therefore does not show the kind's work got easier
  overall; the measure must be per unit of human judgment, not per task.
- **Crossing the context boundary is a cost the run carries; the
  boundary itself is not a price.** The context boundary is a feasibility
  limit
  ([context is scarce for feasibility before cost](../../theory/context-efficiency-is-the-central-design-concern-in-agent-systems.md)),
  so which operations of **G** stay inside one context is metadata of a
  second-kind run, recorded so that comparisons are like for like. Work
  that must cross, through sub-agents, code-managed workflows or
  multi-step processes, pays for coordination machinery and handoff loss
  ([coordination guarantees](../../theory/agent-orchestration-needs-coordination-guarantees-not-just.md);
  ADR 113/118 priced one crossing), and that machinery is counted in the
  total cost the comparison sums. Whether **G** is cheaper than the
  baseline is decided by those figures, not by how much work stays below
  the boundary.
- **Unattended runs make unequal-cost comparison common.** Matched-budget
  comparison of controllers stays valid; where costs differ materially,
  net value with the exchange rate swept is the added option (the
  [Russell–Wefald ingest](../../sources/russell-wefald-principles-of-metareasoning.ingest.md)).
  **G**'s controllers need cost-per-yield records that state the regime
  they ran in before either comparison is possible.
- **The brief's wider claim is not carried.** That economic reasoning is a
  more general organizing principle than epistemology, and the rivalry
  with resource-rational accounts of routinization, are deferred
  (recorded in `kb/log.md`) and are not premises here.

## Operativity and warrant

No consumer yet. What would consume **G** is a second kind of knowledge
work run on Commonplace by an operator who is not its author, through the
installed package and skills (ADR 086's delivery path), with **K_P** as
that project's collections, types and routines. The first-downstream-run
template is the nearest prepared instance, though its task is still KB
building. No oracle is added by this proposal; the ablation proposal's
measures are reused, and their warrant stops where that proposal says.

## Adoption criteria

The proposal reduces to one question: does shared support deliver
comparable outcomes at lower total cost in a second kind of work? The
comparison is made *within* the second kind, against a competent baseline
on the same work, so that architecture is not confounded with task
difficulty.

Evidence that would support the conjecture:

- A second kind of knowledge work runs on the machinery with only **K_P**
  added, and the record counts how much of **G** was reused unmodified,
  how much **K_P** was needed, what maintenance of **G** the second kind
  caused, and what share of the kind's work **G** kept inside one context.
- On the same work, over a fixed horizon, Commonplace support reaches
  outcomes comparable to a competent domain-specific tool or to generic
  harness features alone (option 3), at lower total cost counted as setup,
  operation and maintenance. The ablation proposal's measures supply the
  outcome side; the cost side is the counts above.

Conversion of **G**'s operations from interpreted to mechanical is one
possible source of the savings, not a requirement: shared interpreted
procedures can save authoring, discovery and review effort while staying
interpreted, and making one operation mechanical does not by itself show
net savings.

Evidence that would defeat it, drawn from the failure conditions in the
[bootstrap note](../../theory/a-bootstrap-fits-the-bitter-lesson-only-if-learning-outgrows-it.md)
and the instrument note, restated as cost comparisons:

- The second kind requires a bespoke ontology and evaluator that share
  nothing operative with **G**, so nothing is reused.
- Maintenance of **G** grows with the number of kinds by more than the
  savings the added kinds yield. Growth alone is not failure; growth that
  outweighs savings is.
- The competent baseline reaches comparable outcomes at lower total cost
  over the same horizon.

The trigger for an adoption decision is the first completed second-kind
run with the comparison recorded. One run supports a bounded next step; it
does not establish the claim for every kind. Until then the proposal holds
the conjecture and its defeaters, and the program's successes inside the
KB remain evidence about theory building only.

---

Relevant Notes:

- [An optimal long-run learning strategy invests in its own machinery](../../theory/an-optimal-long-run-learning-strategy-invests-in-its-own-machinery.md) — rests-on: the amortization argument that gives the conjecture its economic form
- [Universal software factory needs a declared universality axis](../../theory/universal-software-factory-needs-a-declared-universality-axis.md) — rests-on: the declarations a generality claim must make, applied here to kinds of knowledge work
- [Agentic substrate needs family-specific machinery to be a factory](../../theory/agentic-substrate-needs-family-specific-machinery-to-be-a-factory.md) — rests-on: the `configure(G, K_P)` form the conjecture borrows
- [A hand-crafted bootstrap fits the Bitter Lesson only if learning can outgrow it](../../theory/a-bootstrap-fits-the-bitter-lesson-only-if-learning-outgrows-it.md) — rests-on: the failure conditions reused as defeaters
- [Codify-versus-LLM decision heuristics](../../theory/codify-versus-llm-decision-heuristics.md) — rests-on: the stake-and-odds rule that bears on building G ahead of its second consumer

name: design-proposal
description: Contract for unadopted Commonplace designs — problem, explanatory case, alternatives, feasibility, and the commitment requested
schema: ./design-proposal.schema.yaml

# Design proposal

## Authoring Instructions

Use a design proposal for a finished but unadopted design: the problem, the option space, the forces, and the free choices — without deciding. A design still being worked out stays in the workshop layer (`kb/work/`); a decided and implemented choice becomes an ADR (`../adr/`). Where proposals may live is a placement rule in [`kb/reference/COLLECTION.md`](../COLLECTION.md); everything a proposal must be is stated here ([ADR 084](../adr/084-kind-rules-live-in-type-specs-and-operations-in-instructions.md)).

- **No adoption decision.** A proposal may recommend a candidate, hold several options, or leave forces unresolved. A recommendation does not authorize adoption. When a choice ships, it becomes an ADR and the proposal leaves the frontier (see Lifecycle).
- **Problem, outcome, and explanatory case.** The opening states the problem, the outcome adoption would seek, and why the candidate changes are expected to produce it. Distinguish current facts, explanatory conjectures, intended outcomes, and candidate choices. An explanation of why an option could work does not establish that it is the only acceptable choice: [explanatory and constructive commitments differ in what they change](../../theory/theory-and-capacity-building-make-the-same-kind-of-commitment.md).
- **Inspectable option space.** Distinguish independently stated boundary commitments, constraints derived from them, local requirements, and open choices. Show materially different alternatives and the consequences that distinguish them; familiar package names alone do not expose the choices they bundle. When a consequential decomposition is itself at issue, include a rival decomposition under the same boundary commitments, or state the unresolved gap if none has been found. A [boundary-preserving rival demotes a claimed constraint to a choice](../../theory/a-framework-rule-with-a-boundary-preserving-rival-is-not-inherited.md); failure to find one proves no necessity. Analytic combinations without a feasibility argument remain unresolved regions, not available options. The map need only expose the differences relevant to this decision, not enumerate every combination ([design-space exploration](../../theory/first-principles-analysis-maps-design-space-before-selection.md)).
- **Detail answers a design question.** Concrete detail, prototype results, field names, schemas, thresholds, or procedures belong when they establish feasibility, distinguish rivals, test an uncertainty, or satisfy a named constraint. Mark illustrative details as non-binding and identify choices still open. Detail does not replace the option space or make an illustrative implementation authoritative. This permits prototypes during exploration while keeping [closure later than exploration](../../theory/first-principles-analysis-maps-design-space-before-selection.md).
- **Transferable theory stays in notes.** A requirement or rationale that forms an independently transferable truth-apt claim belongs in `kb/theory/` and is cited from here via a `rests-on` edge. A proposal to change adopted theory vocabulary belongs in `kb/theory/proposals/`. The design proposal inlines system-specific constraints, candidate options, and the context needed to evaluate them.
- **Dated current-state anchor.** State the system facts the proposal rests on under a `## Current state (as of YYYY-MM-DD)` heading. Going stale against later ADRs is an expected lifecycle event, not a defect: refresh or retire.
- **Operativity and warrant** (proposals authored 2026-07-24 or later). For each option that changes behavior-determining organization, state its operativity path — what would consume the change, through which channel, with what force ([operative change](../../theory/definitions/operative-change.md)). "No consumer yet; one must be built" is a valid answer and exactly what the adoption decision needs to see. If an option adds or strengthens automated evaluation, also name what warrants the oracle and where that warrant stops.
- **Feasibility and commitment scope.** For each candidate presented as adoptable, give a feasibility argument or witness and identify unresolved obstacles, including dependencies on uncertain results. State whether the requested commitment is a bounded probe, reversible trial, routine reliance, or a choice creating costly dependencies. Match support to that scope; neither a successful local trial nor a borrowed design establishes wider applicability ([starting warrant and earned scope](../../theory/derivation-and-inheritance-give-starting-warrant-earns-scope.md)). If reversal would be costly, identify what would depend on the choice, what reversal would disturb, and its warrant: an enduring constraint, discriminating transfer evidence or proof for a stated scope, or [coordination value](../../theory/definitions/coordination-value.md) from actual adopters needing a shared structure. Cheap reversible trials do not require this entrenchment argument ([adoption versus entrenchment](../../theory/current-task-fit-alone-does-not-warrant-costly-entrenchment.md)).
- **Adoption criteria and unresolved choices.** Name what would have to be observed, built, or decided for an option to be adopted, and which unresolved result could change selection, scope, timing, or abandonment. Where a consequential choice is deferred for evidence, identify the alternative that remains feasible, the observation or bounded probe that could change the decision, and the condition that returns it to decision with a follow-on response. A probe names its knowledge gap, cost, output, and stop condition; it must not create the full dependency structure it is meant to evaluate. Account for the cost of waiting and any expiry of the alternative. A promise of more research without these conditions is not [productive deferral](../../theory/productive-deferral-requires-option-evidence-and-convergence.md).
- **Unmistakably proposed.** The description leads with "Proposal:". Readers of `kb/reference/` are usually trying to act on the shipped system, so a proposal never presents shipped behavior as open, or proposed behavior as shipped.

## Frontmatter

| Field | Required | Use |
|---|---:|---|
| `description` | Yes | Leads with `Proposal:`; an archived adopted proposal may use `Proposal (adopted):`. |
| `type` | Yes | `reference/types/design-proposal.md`, including once archived. |
| `tags` | No | Navigation tags. |
| `traits` | No | Review-routing traits, e.g. `has-external-sources`. |

- The schema enforces the `Proposal` lead and the dated current-state heading; the other clauses are checked by type-conformance review.
- Review separates the artifact's regions. Current-state claims answer to the system; explanatory conjectures answer to argument and evidence; candidate choices answer to requirements, constraints, consequences, and trade-offs. Intended outcomes are prospective, not claims of achieved results. Do not flag a stated benefit solely because it has not yet been achieved, or demand hesitant wording solely because an explanation remains conjectural. Criticize its explanatory case, feasibility, or requested commitment rather than automatically deleting or hedging it. Neither confident wording nor tentative wording supplies support.
- Type-conformance review applies the content requirements above without demanding a particular matrix, section layout, or production history. A finished proposal can contain unresolved choices when it makes their consequences and route to resolution inspectable. Claim-title expectations do not apply.

## Lifecycle

A proposal is in one of three states, or has been withdrawn. Each transition has one procedure.

| State | What must hold | Enters by |
|---|---|---|
| **Live** (`kb/reference/proposals/`) | Every clause above. Nothing it contains has shipped. | Promotion from a workshop, or a new proposal written directly |
| **Partially adopted** (still live) | The shipped part is gone from the proposal: shipped behavior is described in reference docs and recorded in an ADR or its implementing commit, and the current-state anchor notes the adoption. A proposal that silently retains shipped content has become a false description. | [Extract the adopted part of a proposal](../../instructions/extract-adopted-part-of-a-proposal.md) |
| **Archived** (`kb/reference/proposals/archive/`) | Fully adopted, or retired by a later decision that forecloses it. Nothing still current remains: shipped behavior, decision-relevant reasoning, and transferable requirements have left, and what stays is the irreproducible remainder — dated current-state anchors and the measurements the design rested on. An ADR names it by title in prose, with no path and no link. The file is frozen: correct it only for link integrity when something it points at moves. | [Retire an artifact](../../instructions/retire-artifact.md) |

**Withdrawn** is the exit for a live proposal whose problem no longer exists in the system, or whose adoption trigger has lapsed, when no decision forecloses it. The operator decides; the withdrawing commit's body names which condition holds and its evidence. Anything still current is extracted first ([ADR 085](../adr/085-withdrawn-proposals-are-deleted.md)).

When a live proposal's current-state anchor may have gone stale, [refresh the proposal's current state](../../instructions/refresh-a-proposal-current-state.md); a refresh routes shipped or foreclosed content to the procedures above and reports a lapsed trigger to the operator.

**Retirement destination: archive to `kb/reference/proposals/archive/` when the proposal is adopted or retired by a decision; delete when it is withdrawn.** Archived files keep this type ([ADR 056](../adr/056-adopted-and-retired-proposals-archive-out-of-the-frontier.md)). [Retire an artifact](../../instructions/retire-artifact.md) reads this line to pick its destination.

name: review-result
description: "One completed gate, conformance or report-method assessment with structured findings and controller-owned execution provenance"
schema: ./review-result.schema.yaml
---

# Review result

A review result records one assessment of captured target text against a criterion. Completion means the output passed deterministic checks, not that its judgment is correct. A report outcome is not a favorable verdict. Use this type for individual gate, compression-check, type-conformance and collection-conformance verdicts, and for critique, composition-friction, premise-decomposition and compression-synthesis reports. Do not use it for combined improvement packets or connection discovery.

## Content

Findings state what the assessed text establishes or fails to establish. Each passage finding quotes enough verbatim text to identify one contiguous span uniquely. A quote is matched after whitespace and typographic quote marks are normalized, so a line wrap in the target does not break it. A quote therefore identifies a passage and is not a byte-exact copy of it. A consumer that needs the exact span locates the quote in the captured target, which holds the exact bytes. A document-wide or absence finding explains the condition without inventing a quotation. Finding levels belong to verdict criteria; critique reports instead state whether the strongest attack lands and how the note engages it. An empty findings list is an honest completed result when no finding remains.

The body explains the assessment without repeating every structured finding. A critique preserves its central commitment, critique mode, strongest case, the note's response and constructive findings, including why an attack does not survive. Low-confidence no-surviving-attack findings leave the need for a domain check visible.

Each report method has its own shape, which the schema checks by the result's `criterion`:

| Method | Findings | Required body |
|---|---|---|
| Critique | constructive findings | `attack-outcome` in frontmatter; `## Strongest case against it`, `## How the note engages it`, `## Constructive findings` |
| Composition friction | the surfaced joints, thinnest first; each reason begins `UNSUPPORTED`, `THIN` or `HOLDS` | a `**Filter:** SURVIVES` or `DISSOLVES` line; `## Filter`, `## Thinnest joints`, `## For the human` |
| Premise decomposition | one per premise; each reason begins `HOLDS`, `DOUBTFUL` or `DEFEATED`, and a non-`HOLDS` reason names `LOCAL` or `GLOBAL` and `instance`, `prevalence` or `priced-exception` | a `**Register:**` line; `## Premises and counterexamples`, `## For the human` |
| Compression synthesis | zero to three opportunities | `## Opportunities` |

Only critique supplies `attack-outcome`. Friction's filter line and the premise statuses route attention; they are not overall verdicts. A report criterion is named by its library instruction's identity, so moving one of these instructions requires a schema edit.

## Field ownership

The worker fragment supplies only `type`, `findings`, `outcome`, optional `attack-outcome`, and the body. Findings precede the outcome so the serialized verdict follows its rationale. The fragment is not a complete saved artifact. The controller completes and validates it; workers never assert hashes, execution identities or timestamps.

| Fields | Owner and meaning |
|---|---|
| `type`, `findings`, `outcome`, `attack-outcome` | Worker assessment; findings contain `scope`, `quotes`, `reason`, and `level` for verdicts |
| `description`, `format`, `contract` | Controller's result-format identity and expected verdict/report contract |
| `note`, `criterion` | Original target and criterion identities |
| `note-sha256`, `criterion-sha256` | Freshness hashes; the note hash may cover normalized watched parts, not exact bytes |
| `target-sha256`, `target-capture` | Exact assessed UTF-8 bytes and their retained repository-relative location |
| `observation`, `contract-sha256` | Execution observation and captured output-contract identity |
| `profile`, `model`, `run`, `launch`, `completed-at` | Requested execution configuration and observed execution provenance |
| `raw-output`, `raw-output-sha256` | Retained original worker fragment, distinct from this completed artifact |

## Template

Worker fragment for a verdict criterion; code supplies the remaining fields:

```markdown
---
type: types/review-result.md
findings:
  - scope: document
    quotes: []
    reason: "The claim omits the condition needed for its stated conclusion."
    level: warn
outcome: warn
---

# Review

## Summary

The conclusion needs its missing condition.
```

A critique fragment uses `outcome: report`, supplies `attack-outcome`, and omits finding levels. Its body retains the critique instruction's sections. Other report fragments use `outcome: report`, omit `attack-outcome` and finding levels, and follow their instruction's Output section. Neither fragment uses a terminal `## Result:` line. Operational production and publication belong to the review command, not to this type.
contracts.reports/COLLECTION.md:
---
type: types/collection-contract.md
---

# Writing conventions for kb/reports/ (report collection)

## Purpose and scope

This collection contains analytical outputs, evaluation records, and local
operational evidence that are consumed as reports rather than as library
claims or system definitions. Placement here is justified by the output's
retention policy and consumer, not by its filename or by the fact that a tool
generated it.

A report belongs here only when a named operation consumes the report itself.
Transferable claims belong in `kb/theory/`; descriptions of the shipped system
and its decisions belong in `kb/reference/`; executable procedures belong in
`kb/instructions/`; and reasoning whose value is consumed by unfinished work
belongs in `kb/work/`.

## Policy areas

Every report artifact lives in exactly one first-level policy area:

| Area | Retention policy | Typical contents |
|---|---|---|
| `state/` | Ignored, one directory per producing workflow. Not disposable merely because it was generated: the owning workflow decides when an output may be removed, and the [state README](./state/README.md) states per workflow what deletion loses. | Review results, packets and runs; fix dispositions; ingest working directories; connect, critique, friction, premise-decomposition and promotion-candidate reports. |
| `retained/` | Durable report records kept with the project. Payloads are tracked. | Evaluation corpora, experiment reports, measurements, and exact records cited by later work. |
| `types/` | Collection-local structural contracts, not report payloads. | Optional project-authored report contracts; command-produced generic report types are global. |

The published site includes `retained/` and leaves out `state/`. Inside `retained/`, a subtree carrying a
`.commonplace-validation-ignore` marker is left out of the site as well as
validation; mark exact captures and trial bundles so, keeping the report that
interprets them published.

Do not put report payloads directly at the collection root. Moving an artifact
between policy areas is a change in its retention contract, not a filing-only
rename.

## Quality goal

Make the report sufficient for the operation that consumes it without making
it impersonate a durable knowledge claim. State the subject, inputs or source
state, method, result, and material limits to the degree needed to interpret
or reproduce the output. Record the model and prompt or instruction identity
when an LLM judgment is part of the evidence and the producing workflow does
not already retain them.

`state/` must satisfy the owning workflow's authority, integrity, and cleanup
rules. `retained/` must remain
understandable from a clean checkout without relying on ignored files.

## Titles, descriptions, and exact records

- Use a title that names the analysis, experiment, or result. A title such as
  "Report" does not distinguish the artifact.
- When frontmatter is present, write a retrieval-oriented `description` that
  identifies the subject and why the exact output is retained.
- Frontmatter-free Markdown is permitted for deliberate unstructured output.
- Preserve an exact capture when fidelity is the report's purpose. If a copied
  artifact carries another collection's local type only as captured data, put
  a `.commonplace-validation-ignore` marker at the capture-set root rather than
  presenting that copy as a live typed artifact of this collection.

## Maintenance semantics

- A state producer owns cleanup and states, in the state README, what deleting
  its output loses: nothing unique (rebuild from retained inputs), one paid
  judgment (rerun when needed) or current coverage, an unresolved disposition
  or decision evidence (preserve). Generated state may contain non-reproducible
  judgments or the only current disposition, so Git ignore status never
  licenses deletion.
- A retained report is changed according to its declared role. Correct a
  living report in place; preserve a dated or frozen observation as an exact
  record and create a new observation when the measured state changes.
- Local evidence notes are the one interpreted form `retained/` keeps as
  durable artifacts: a `types/note.md` artifact whose bounded inference
  concerns only Commonplace's own choices or their measured effects, beside
  the raw records it interprets. Its formal edges use this collection's labels
  below. An inference that keeps a free variable belongs in
  `kb/theory/evidence/`.
- If a report develops a transferable claim, binding rule, system premise, or
  unfinished-work lifecycle, extract that content to its proper collection.
  Do not broaden `retained/` into a second notes, reference, instructions, or
  workshop collection.

## Outbound links

Reports may inspect any project surface. Use relative Markdown links for live
navigation and state in prose why the target matters. Inline links may carry
ordinary evidential or procedural context. Footer-shaped formal edges use this
small authorized set:

| label | destinations | reader need |
|---|---|---|
| `derived-from` | sources, external | inspect the source material from which the report was produced |
| `is-evidence-for` | theory, reference, reports | inspect the durable claim, decision, or report record on which this output bears |
| `compares-with` | theory, reference, sources, reports | compare two artifacts on a named shared axis |
| `see-also` | any durable collection, external | inspect useful adjacent context when no stronger relation applies |

The destination collection separately decides whether it may author a
reciprocal edge. A formal edge into this collection targets `retained/`;
`state/` may be mentioned inline only as local operational context.

Tracked library artifacts must not depend on an ignored `state/` file being
present. Summarize the needed evidence in the tracked artifact or
promote the exact report to `retained/` first. Tracked artifacts may cite a
`retained/` report when the exact record is useful to their reader.

## Validation markers

The tracked `.commonplace-validation-ignore` marker at `state/` excludes its
data-bearing subtree from collection-scoped validation. The marker does not
hide files from ordinary discovery, and explicit validation of
one typed report still applies its type contract.

A file under `state/` may declare any valid type spec, including another
collection's local type. Workflows stage candidates there for other
collections, and a candidate must validate against its destination's contract.
The type spec itself stays in the owning collection's `types/` directory.
`retained/` does not share this exception.

## What does not belong here

- A generated explanation or synthesis whose claim should survive the run →
  `kb/theory/` or `kb/reference/` according to its consumer.
- A procedure named "report" because it produces one → `kb/instructions/`.
- Drafts, deliberation, and run traces consumed by an unfinished investigation
  → `kb/work/`.
- External source captures and their durable analyses → `kb/sources/`.
- Build outputs with no report consumer → their build cache, not `kb/reports/`.
